Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:73: We shall complete this gate with the level of the penitent. They said in Vayikra Rabbah (7:2), in these words: From where do we learn that for one who repents, it is accounted to him as if he had gone up to Jerusalem and built the Temple and the altar, and offered upon it all the sacrifices of the Torah? As it is said, "The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit" (Psalms 51:19).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:74: They also said in the Midrash (Psalms 18) on the psalm "For the leader, upon Shoshannim, of the sons of Korach" (Psalms 45:1), in these words: Whoever repents of a transgression in his hand, the Holy One, blessed be He, further calls him by a beloved name. Come and see with the sons of Korach: before they repented they were not called "lilies" (shoshannim) and "beloved" (yedidim); after they repented they were called shoshannim and yedidim, as it is said, "Upon Shoshannim, a maskil, a song of loves." So too David: before he repented he was not written in the roster above; after he repented he was written in the roster above and was called "servant," as it is said, "For the leader, of the servant of the Lord, of David" (Psalms 18:1).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:75: Also concerning the level of repentance, it is explained in the Yerushalmi (Ta'anit ch.4): it is written, "And rend your heart and not your garments, and return to the Lord your God, for He is gracious and merciful" (Joel 2:13). Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: if you rend your heart in repentance, you need not rend your garments — not for your sons and not for your daughters, but for the Lord your God. Why? "For He is gracious and merciful, slow to anger and abounding in kindness, and relents from bringing evil."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:76: And with this this gate is concluded, with a soul at rest and satisfied (nafshi vetzivi). May God grant us the merit to be among those who perform complete repentance before Him, with love and awe. So may it be His will, Amen, selah, forever.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 1:1: The matter of holiness — we were commanded concerning it in the Torah several times. The first is at the end of Parashat Shemini: "And you shall sanctify yourselves and be holy, for I am holy..." (Leviticus 11:44). And likewise in Parashat Kedoshim it is mentioned three times: the first, at the beginning of the portion, "You shall be holy, for I am holy" (Leviticus 19:2); then, "And you shall sanctify yourselves and be holy, for I am the Lord your God" (Leviticus 20:7); and at the end of the portion, "And you shall be holy unto Me, for I the Lord am holy, and have separated you from the peoples to be Mine" (Leviticus 20:26). And in the portion of tzitzit: "That you may remember and do all My commandments, and be holy unto your God" (Numbers 15:40). Further, in Parashat Emor el HaKohanim: "And you shall not profane My holy Name, but I will be sanctified among the children of Israel" (Leviticus 22:32) — and this is the positive commandment to sanctify His Name in public, as will be explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 1:2: Since this statement of "You shall be holy" appears in the Torah so many times, even though it is not itself one of the core 248 positive commandments, nevertheless it is the root for performing all the commandments for the sake of the One who commanded them. For once a person is holy and separated from attachment to the love of this world, he will strive to do the will of his Maker in truth, and will bind himself to His love, blessed be He, to perform His commandments with desire and love — for what does this world and its benefits mean to him? — as will be explained, please God, regarding the ways of holiness. Therefore it is repeated in the Torah so many times, because of the great benefit that will come from it to the soul.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 1:3: The reason for the essence of holiness our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained in Tanchuma (beginning of Parashat Kedoshim), in these words: This is what is written, "And the Lord of Hosts is exalted through justice, and the holy God is sanctified through righteousness" (Isaiah 5:16) — He is sanctified in His world through righteousness, which teaches merit on behalf of Israel, as it is said, "I speak in righteousness" (Isaiah 63:1).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 1:4: The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel: In the future I shall be sanctified through you, as it is said, "For when he sees his children..." (Isaiah 29:23), and likewise it says of Israel, "You in whom I take glory" (Isaiah 49:3). You are sanctified through Me, and I am sanctified through you, as it is said, "You shall be holy, for I am holy" (Leviticus 19:2).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 1:5: The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel: Before I created you, the ministering angels were praising and sanctifying Me by you, saying, "Blessed is the Lord, the God of Israel, from world to world" (Psalms 106:48). Once Adam was created, they said, "This is he by whose name we praise You." He said to them, "This one is a thief," as it is said, "And she ate of the tree..." (Genesis 3:17). Noah came; they said to Him, "This is he." He said to them, "This one is a drunkard," as it is said, "And he drank of the wine" (Genesis 9:21). Abraham came; they said to Him, "This is he." He said to them, "This one is a convert (a stranger)." Isaac came; they said to Him, "This is he." He said to them, "This one loves My enemies (Esau)." Jacob came; they said to Him, "This is he." He said to them, "Yes," and so it says, "Your name shall no longer be called Jacob, but Israel shall be your name" (Genesis 35:10), and all of Israel were called by his name. At that hour the Holy One, blessed be He, sanctified Israel unto His Name, as it is said, "Israel, in whom I take glory" (Isaiah 49:3).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 1:6: The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel: Since you have been sanctified unto My Name before I created the world, be holy as I am holy, as it is said, "You shall be holy, for I am holy." To what may this be compared? To a king who betrothed a woman; he said to her, "Since you have been sanctified unto My Name, I am king and you are queen — just as My honor is such, so is your honor, since you are My wife." So too the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Moses, "Sanctify the people for Me," as it is said, "Go to the people and sanctify them today and tomorrow" (Exodus 19:10) — sanctify them. The Holy One, blessed be He, came and said to them, "And you shall be to Me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation" (Exodus 19:6). Why? "For I the Lord am holy" — you too shall be holy, just as I have sanctified you unto My Name, as it is said, "Speak to the whole congregation of the children of Israel and say to them: You shall be holy."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 1:7: Now although this statement is profound, and it contains several subtleties that every student needs to examine carefully, nevertheless in this composition we have come only to explain what pertains to practical matters.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 1:8: Regarding what the Holy One, blessed be He, said, "You are sanctified through Me, and I am sanctified through you" — the matter is that first we are sanctified through Him, drawing holiness from Him to us, so that we may become sanctified through the performance of the commandments; and afterward He is sanctified through us, through the arousal from below that ascends from our deeds. And the reason is that all things require arousal from below, as we explained several times, and as will be explained further below in the statement "May He send your help from the sanctuary."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 1:9: "The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel: Before I created you..." — now the text comes to give the reason how Israel can reach such a supernal level and draw from the mystery of the supernal holiness, for on the surface they would seem to have no hold above. Hence it gives the reason concerning the angels who were praising the Holy One, blessed be He, before man was created, saying "the God of Israel," and when Jacob came, the Holy One, blessed be He, said to them, "This is Israel." And the matter is as explained in the Zohar (Parashat Bereshit 24a), in Ra'aya Meheimna (Parashat Mishpatim 119a), and in the Tikkunim (102a): the mystery of "Israel arose in thought," which is the mystery of the son drawn forth from the mind of Abba (the supernal Father), and from this reality is the root of the souls of Israel; and Jacob was their root in his supernal reality called "Israel." And even though we say, "You are children to the Lord your God" (Deuteronomy 14:1), the intent is that when the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah are united, the souls are drawn from above, from the mind of Abba and Imma, and it follows accordingly that the source of the souls is from the place of holiness.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 1:10: And what is meant by "At that hour the Holy One, blessed be He, sanctified Israel unto His Name, as it is said, 'Israel, in whom I take glory'" — the intent is that the souls of Israel are held fast within His Name, the Name YHVH; and the proof is that as long as Israel are in exile, the Name is not whole, as it is said, "For a hand is upon the throne of Yah" (Exodus 17:16). And the reason may perhaps be said according to what is written in the Tikkunim (86b): "Let the heavens rejoice and the earth be glad" — Yod-Heh is in the heavens, Vav-Heh is on the earth; and since the Shechinah is in exile and our souls are bound to her, the exile, which is the kelipah (shell), separates, and the Name is not bound together as one. This is what the verse means, "Israel, in whom I take glory" — His glory is that His Name should be whole. And since the root of the souls preceded the world, as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Yalkut Isaiah 452), "In the beginning God created" (Genesis 1:1) — for the sake of Israel, who are called "the beginning" — therefore when the angels were praising Him, it was because He was destined to be called "the God of Israel" openly. This is the meaning of "Blessed is the Lord, the God of Israel" — then He is influenced, blessed, and He is sanctified from above through us. This is the meaning of "Since you have been sanctified unto My Name," and this is what is said: "The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel: Since you have been sanctified unto My Name before I created you."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 1:11: And the intent of the phrase "Since you have been sanctified unto My Name" is as stated in the passage above, that the angels were saying "Blessed is the Lord, the God of Israel" — that His unique Name, YHVH, was designated and united specifically with them; it follows that they are sanctified, separated, and made ready for His Name.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 1:12: And this is what is meant by the careful wording at the end of the passage: "You too shall be holy, as it is said, 'Speak to the whole congregation of the children of Israel... you shall be holy'" — since they are called Israel, it is fitting that they be holy, for the reason explained: that the Name YHVH is called upon us, and He takes glory and is sanctified through it and is called "the God of Israel" — meaning that His Godhood is revealed through Israel; and had there, God forbid, been no Israel, there would be no world, and His Godhood and glory would not be revealed to created beings. This is the meaning of "For I the Lord am your God" — meaning, the God that is yours, the God of Israel, in that through you My Godhood is revealed.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 1:13: And by this [we understand] the statement "Since you have been sanctified unto My Name" — it is the mystery of "Israel is holy unto the Lord" (Jeremiah 2:3), meaning that the sanctification of Israel from the mystery of holiness is for the sake of YHVH, who is Tiferet, so that they may be a vessel to receive His holiness; they must be holy like Him. It is like the analogy of a groom who sanctifies (betroths) the bride, saying to her, "You shall be sanctified unto me" — just as he is holy and she is to be his, so his wife who joins with him must also be holy; for otherwise they would have no fitting bond to join with one another. This is the parable given: "To what may this be compared? To a king who betrothed a woman..."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 1:14: By this we can understand the end of the verse, "For I the Lord your God am holy" — the phrase "your God" points to what is required: since He is our God and His Shechinah rests upon us specifically, it is fitting that we have within us the readiness for Him to be, so to speak, our God, and for His holiness to rest upon us. Therefore we must strip ourselves of matters of materiality, for all matters of materiality are from the side of the kelipah; and when we sanctify ourselves, this becomes the cause for us to cleave to Him. This is the meaning of "And you shall be holy unto your God" — meaning, be holy so that you may cleave to your God and God may rest within you; for you have no bond by which He may rest within you and you within Him except through the side of holiness — for behold, He is holy and spiritual, and you are physical, so how can the spiritual rest and cleave to the physical? Only through the side of holiness and separation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 1:15: And they illustrated this matter with a fine parable in the Midrash (Vayikra Rabbah, Parashat Kedoshim 24:7). Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman said: A parable of a High Priest who was walking on the road, and a certain shopkeeper happened upon him and said, "Let me go with you." He said to him, "I am a son of a priest, and I walk on a pure path, and it is not my way to walk among graves. If you go with me, well and good; and if not, in the end I will leave you and go on my own." So too Moses said to Israel, "For the Lord your God walks in the midst of your camp to save you" (Deuteronomy 23:15). This is also the meaning of the parable in the passage before us, which says, "Just as My honor is such, so is your honor" — the meaning being that His honor, blessed be He, is certainly in His holiness; and indeed we find that "holy" and "honor" are one and the same matter — "and honor the Holy One of the Lord" (Isaiah 58:13).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 1:16: The pivot around which this passage revolves is this: that the supernal unification cannot be brought about except through arousal from the souls. The proof is what is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Bereshit 35a) on "And a mist went up from the earth" (Genesis 2:6): the reason Adam and his wife were created back to back is that there was no arousal from below to bring about the union above face to face; and once there are souls below, "a mist went up from the earth" — that is the arousal from below — afterward "and watered the whole face of the ground." This is what the angels meant by saying "Blessed is the Lord, the God of Israel" — meaning, blessed is the Lord; and "blessed" means influenced (flowing) from the source of blessings, which comes about through His Godhood resting within Israel, hence He is called "the God of Israel."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 1:17: And the supernal unification cannot come about except through holy souls, and these are the souls of the righteous, whose souls are always attached above and who are separated from the vanities of this world, as is said in Parashat Terumah (134b), and as we quoted in the Gate of Love (ch. 9), in these words: Fortunate are the righteous who know how to set their will toward the supernal holy King, and all their desire is not for this world, and it is with longing that their will is nullified [toward this world]; rather they know and strive to set their will and to attach themselves above, etc. Now the Holy One, blessed be He, is holy and set apart from the physicality and lowliness of the world, and there is no comparison to His holiness and spirituality, as we say (the hymn Yigdal), "We cannot compare His holiness to anything." Therefore the righteous who unify His unity must be separated from materiality and holy with a holiness of the mind, which is the root of all forms of holiness, preceding them all and coming last after them all, as will be explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 1:18: This is the meaning of "And you shall be holy men unto Me" (Exodus 22:30) — for "holy" refers to the supernal holiness in the mystery of thought, and our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained: "When you are men of holiness, you are Mine" — meaning, belonging to Me. And holiness of the mind cannot come about except through a person's separating himself from the desires of the world, especially from marital relations, which is what disqualifies the mind. And to confirm this truth: before Adam was created, the angels were praising and saying, "Blessed is the Lord, the God of Israel" — for through the holy souls of Israel He is blessed from the source of blessings.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 1:19: And it is possible to add an embellishment here: it is known that YHVH includes ten [sefirot], and the Name Elohai numerically equals ten (by the small reckoning), and the Name Elohai is in the Shechinah — these are the "ten, ten shekels, by the shekel of the sanctuary" (Numbers 7:86); and Yisrael also numerically equals ten (by the small reckoning); and there is no holiness (kedushah, a quorum for sanctification) with fewer than ten (Berachot 21b). It follows that the souls of Israel are sanctified, and they are the vessel and sheath for the supernal holiness. Thus it is impossible for there to be unification above in the ten [sefirot] except through the souls of Israel; when they are holy, then the ten are unified in the emanation of the King, so that He and His life-force become one within them.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 1:20: And when Adam was created, who was the handiwork of the Holy One, blessed be He, such that people thought he was a god, on account of the loftiness of his soul, and likewise his body, which shone, as they said (Vayikra Rabbah 20:2) that the heel of Adam's foot dimmed the orb of the sun — the angels thought that from him would come the chain of the souls of Israel, who are called "Israel is holy unto the Lord, the first-fruits" (Jeremiah 2:3), and it was concerning him that they were praising, "Blessed is the Lord, the God of Israel." But once he sinned, they said, "This one is a thief," and so on, until Jacob came, whose stock was holy and whose bed was complete with twelve holy tribes; then Israel were sanctified unto His Name, that the unification would be performed through them, and they would be the sheath to receive the holiness. This is the meaning of "Since you have been sanctified unto My Name," and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 1:21: And at the giving of the Torah, when the Holy One, blessed be He, wished to cause His Shechinah to rest among them so that they might attain the levels of prophecy — and this was not possible while they were still partaking in matters of physicality — He therefore said, "Go to the people and sanctify them today and tomorrow, and let them wash their garments" (Exodus 19:10); and through purity and holiness the supernal spirituality would rest upon them, and they would be able to cleave to Him and attain the vision of the supernal sights in prophecy. And first the holiness of the body must precede, and afterward the holiness of the mind would rest upon them; and therefore the Holy One, blessed be He, did not immediately say, "And you shall be to Me a kingdom of priests and men of holiness," for "men of holiness" is holiness of the mind; rather He said, "and a holy nation" — that they be holy with holiness of the body, through separation from physical desires, whether in the holiness of foods or the holiness [of restraint] from forbidden relations, all of which are termed holiness — and by this their bodies are sanctified, and afterward, upon this holiness, the holiness of the mind comes to rest.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 1:22: And what emerges from the totality of this discourse is: first, as to why we must sanctify ourselves — it is explained in the passage with which we began, concerning "You shall be holy": that the entire creation of the souls of Israel is so that they may become holy and cleave to God; for before the world was created they were sanctified, and the Name of the Holy One, blessed be He, was united to them: "the God of Israel." And if we become holy, we are bound to Him and we are called, like Him, "a congregation of holy ones." And so the author of the Tanchuma passage concludes, saying: The Holy One, blessed be He, said to them, "If you merit it, you are called 'a congregation of holy ones'; if you do not merit it, you are called 'an evil congregation,' as it is said, 'How long shall I bear with this evil congregation'" (Numbers 14:27). And we have already explained above the reason for the essence of holiness, by way of the parable of the king who betrothed the woman.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 1:23: Further, the passage explains the reason for holiness: that the Holy One, blessed be He, is sanctified through us and we through Him. And likewise in the passage from the Zohar (Parashat Terumah 133a), it says that there is no holiness above except if there is holiness below. And so it is further stated in the Midrash Tanchuma below (Parashat Kedoshim, section 9), in these words: "Holy ones" — this is what is written, "May He send your help from the sanctuary (mikodesh), and support you from Zion" (Psalms 20:3). "May He send your help from the sanctuary" — from the sanctification of your deeds; "and support you from Zion" — from your deeds [in] Zion. It is made clear that first we sanctify above, "Holy, holy, holy" — this is "And I will be sanctified among the children of Israel" — and afterward He, blessed be He, bestows from His supernal holiness upon us — this is "I the Lord who sanctifies you" — and from that holiness a garment is made for the soul, as it says, "to spread the spreading-out of holiness over it." This is comparable to the fulfillment of a positive commandment, which makes a garment for the soul, as explained — and this is the second aspect of holiness, that of doing good.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 1:24: We have already explained above the reason for arousal from below, in chapter 5, and we likewise explained in the preceding chapters, and in the Gate of Awe, the relation of a person, whether to cause a blemish above or to bring repair — all of it is from the side of the soul; and since the soul is a part of Him, for "a part of the Lord is His people," He cleaves to us and we cleave to Him. Therefore, when a person sanctifies himself, he sanctifies his soul and sanctifies the supernal root, the place from which the soul was drawn forth. And likewise, from the side of the form of his body, which was fashioned through His great Name YHVH, blessed and exalted be He, as it is said in the Tikkunim (131b) that YHVH is to be found in every single limb — and we quoted its wording below, in chapter 7.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 1:25: It follows that when a person sanctifies each and every one of his limbs, he sanctifies the very YHVH that is within him. This is what they said in the Torat Kohanim (beginning of Parashat Kedoshim), in these words: "You shall be holy" — you shall be separated; "you shall be holy, for I am holy" — if you sanctify yourselves, I account it to you as though you had sanctified Me. Or perhaps it means that if you sanctify Me, I am indeed sanctified, and if not, I am not sanctified? The verse teaches, "For I am holy" — in My own holiness I remain, whether they sanctify [themselves] or whether they do not sanctify [themselves].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 1:26: Now, having explained the reason for the necessity of holiness, we shall explain the general essence of holiness, according to what is found in the words of the commentators and the words of Rashbi (Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai), peace be upon him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 1:27: The Ramban (Parashat Kedoshim) wrote, in these words: "You shall be holy" — separated from forbidden relations and from transgression, for wherever you find a fence against forbidden relations, you find holiness — this is Rashi's language. But in the Torat Kohanim I found it stated plainly, "You shall be separated," and so they taught there: "And you shall sanctify yourselves and be holy, for I the Lord am holy" — just as I am holy, so you shall be holy; just as I am separated, so you shall be separated. In my opinion, however, this separation does not mean separating from forbidden relations, as the Rav [Rashi] says, but rather the separation mentioned everywhere in the Talmud, where those who practice it are called perushim (separatists). The matter is that the Torah warned against forbidden relations and forbidden foods, but permitted relations between a man and his wife, and eating meat and drinking wine. If so, one given to desire could find room to be immersed in lust with his wife, or with many wives, and to be among winebibbers and gluttonous eaters of meat, and to speak as he pleases with all manner of vulgarity — since this prohibition was not mentioned explicitly in the Torah — and thus he would be a vile person with the permission of the Torah! Therefore, after detailing the forbidden things it prohibited outright, the verse comes with a general command that we be separated from that which is permitted: one should reduce marital relations, in the manner of what they said, that Torah scholars should not be [constantly] with their wives like roosters, and should engage in it only as much as is necessary to fulfill the commandment. And one should sanctify himself with regard to wine, in its reduction, just as the verse calls the Nazirite "holy"; and he should remember the evils mentioned concerning it in the Torah regarding Noah and Lot. Likewise he should separate himself from impurity even though we were not warned against it explicitly in the Torah, in the manner mentioned that the garments of an am ha'aretz (common person) are deemed as if trodden upon by a zav for the perushim; just as the Nazirite is called "holy" for guarding himself also from the impurity of the dead. Likewise he should guard his mouth and tongue from becoming defiled by excessive gross eating and from vile speech, as the verse mentions, "and every mouth speaks vileness" (Isaiah 9:16); and he should sanctify himself in this until he reaches [the level of] separation, as they said of Rabbi Chiyya, that he never spoke idle talk in his life. In these and similar matters we say that this general commandment came after all the transgressions that are absolutely forbidden had been detailed, so that this general instruction of cleanliness would also include cleanliness of one's hands and body, as it says, "And you shall sanctify yourselves and be holy" — "and you shall sanctify yourselves" refers to the first washing of the hands [before a meal], "and be holy" refers to the second washing, "for holy" refers to fragrant oil — for even though these practices are of rabbinic origin, the essential point of the verse warns of the like of these, that we should be clean, pure, and separated from the masses of people who soil themselves with permitted excesses and with unseemly things. And this is the way of the Torah, to detail and then to generalize in such matters — for after the warning of the particular laws of judges and all dealings between people, "You shall not rob," "You shall not steal," "You shall not defraud," and the other warnings, it says in general, "And you shall do that which is right and good" (Deuteronomy 6:18), that one should enter into the practice of uprightness and equity, and all that is beyond the strict letter of the law, to please one's fellow, as I shall explain when I reach that place, please God. Likewise regarding the Sabbath, it forbade the [thirty-nine] labors with a specific prohibition, and burdensome exertions with a general positive commandment, as it is said, "You shall cease" (tishbot) — and I shall explain this further, please God. And the reason the verse says, "For I the Lord your God am holy," is to say that we shall merit to cleave to Him by being holy — so far his words. And the sum of his words is that the essence of holiness is separation from all the matters of this world that are among the permitted things.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 1:28: What appears to us in explaining the general essence of holiness is this: holiness has two aspects. The first is the aspect of separation, as the Ramban explained, and it is [the meaning of] "kadesh" as a term of separation, of setting a fence and a boundary so as not to go out beyond the bounds into the domain of the mundane. From this category, one finds in the Torah and the Prophets many words of holiness that indicate this — among them, "Set bounds about the mountain and sanctify it" (Exodus 19:23), and likewise "Go to the people and sanctify them today and tomorrow..." (Exodus 19:10), where the intent was that they should sanctify themselves by separating from their wives, as it says, "Be ready for the third day; do not approach a woman" (Exodus 19:15), and many similar instances. This is the aspect of "turn away from evil," corresponding to the negative commandments.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 1:29: There is a second aspect of holiness, which is the drawing down of the holy light upon us, so that we may be enveloped and clothed in that holiness; and this corresponds to "do good."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 1:30: And the proof of this is what they said, of blessed memory, in Tanchuma, in Parashat Tzitzit, on the verse "and you shall be holy unto your God" (Numbers 15:40), in these words: When you perform the commandments, you are sanctified, and your fear is upon the nations; when you cease from the commandments, you become profaned — so far their words. And so it is likewise said in the Mechilta on the verse "And you shall be men of holiness unto Me" (Exodus 22:30), in these words: Isi ben Yehudah says, when the Omnipresent innovates a commandment for Israel, He adds to them holiness — so far his words. Here it is made clear that performing a commandment sanctifies the person and adds holiness to him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 1:31: The matter is that performing a commandment makes a garment of light for the soul, as is explained in the Zohar in several places, that in that garment it is clothed in the lower Garden of Eden. Therefore, in performing the commandment, one sanctifies himself, and therefore we say in the blessing over the fulfillment of the commandments, "who has sanctified us with His commandments" — for the performance of the commandment sanctifies the soul and clothes it in a new light.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 1:32: And there are several particulars that draw holiness upon a person through the fulfillment of the commandments of tzitzit and tefillin, as they, of blessed memory, explained, and as will be explained further.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 1:33: Likewise, regarding the Kedushah that we sanctify each day, "Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of Hosts, the whole earth is full of His glory" — Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (Zohar, Parashat Emor 93a) that the intent of the Kedushah is for each and every one to draw down upon himself from the supernal holiness. And these are his words: And all this is to bring down holiness from above to below, for each one to sanctify himself with this holiness, and to take for himself the spreading-out of a spreading of holiness over him; and this is the mystery of "And I will be sanctified among the children of Israel" first, and afterward, "I am the Lord who sanctifies you" — so far his words. And he explained further, that in the words "the whole earth [is full of] His glory," one should intend to draw the holiness upon himself. It is thus made clear that first we sanctify above, "Holy, holy, holy" — and this is "And I will be sanctified among the children of Israel" — and afterward He, blessed be He, bestows from His supernal holiness upon us — this is "I the Lord who sanctifies you" — and from that holiness a garment is made for the soul, as he said, "to spread the spreading-out of holiness over him." And this is found to be like the matter of the fulfillment of a positive commandment, which makes a garment for the soul, as explained; and this is the second aspect of holiness, that of doing good.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 1:34: And it is possible that these two aspects are what is intended in the Mechilta by saying, "Just as I am holy, so shall you be holy; just as I am separated, so shall you be separated."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 1:35: And with this, this chapter is concluded:
